sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
sources.authors: Prithvi Rajasekaran, Ethan Dixon, Carly Ryan, Jeremy Hadfield
sources.summary: Frames context as a finite attention budget and lays out curation techniques for long-running agents.
keyPoints: Recall from context declines as token count grows (context rot); aim for the smallest set of high-signal tokens.
Clearing old tool results is described as the lightest-touch form of compaction.
Compaction risks dropping details whose importance only shows up later.
Sub-agents should return a condensed summary, often 1,000-2,000 tokens; external notes files carry state across resets.

sources.title: Writing effective tools for agents — with agents
sources.authors: Ken Aizawa et al.
sources.summary: Guidance on designing agent tools, with a section on keeping tool responses token-efficient.
keyPoints: "we restrict tool responses to 25,000 tokens by default" in Claude Code.
Recommends pagination, range selection, filtering and truncation with sensible defaults.
A concise response mode used about a third of the tokens of the detailed mode.
Too many or overlapping tools distract agents from efficient strategies.

sources.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
sources.authors: Jeremy Hadfield, Barry Zhang, Kenneth Lien, Florian Scholz, Jeremy Fox, Daniel Ford
sources.summary: Lessons from Anthropic's orchestrator/sub-agent research system, including cost and coordination failures.
keyPoints: Subagents compress: each explores in its own window and returns the most important tokens.
Agents use ~4x the tokens of chat; multi-agent systems ~15x.
"without detailed task descriptions, agents duplicate work, leave gaps".
Subagents can write outputs to external storage and pass lightweight references back to cut copying overhead.

sources.title: Building effective agents
sources.authors: Erik Schluntz, Barry Zhang
sources.summary: Argues for simple, composable agent designs and careful agent-computer interface (tool) design.
keyPoints: Agentic systems trade latency and cost for task performance; add complexity only when it pays.
Tool definitions deserve as much prompt-engineering care as the main prompt.
Choose tool formats that avoid needless overhead for the model.

sources.title: Best practices for Claude Code
sources.summary: Official Claude Code guidance built around the constraint that the context window fills fast and performance degrades as it fills.
keyPoints: CLAUDE.md loads every session; keep it concise and prune it — "Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions!"
Exclude things Claude can infer from code, file-by-file descriptions, and frequently changing information.
Use /clear between unrelated tasks; a clean session with a better prompt usually beats a long corrected one.
Use subagents so broad investigation does not consume the main context; hooks are deterministic while CLAUDE.md is advisory.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project (CLAUDE.md, rules, auto memory)
sources.summary: Reference for CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md loading, path-scoped rules, auto memory and instruction troubleshooting.
keyPoints: Target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md; longer files consume more context and reduce adherence; imports still load at launch.
Rules with `paths` frontmatter load only when Claude reads matching files.
"if two rules contradict each other, Claude may pick one arbitrarily"; audits flag references to files that don't exist and outdated instructions.
Auto memory loads the first 200 lines / 25KB of MEMORY.md each session; CLAUDE.md is delivered as a user message and is not enforced.

sources.title: Manage costs effectively
sources.summary: Explains where Claude Code token spend comes from and concrete ways to reduce it.
keyPoints: Each request re-sends the full conversation, so a one-line question in a long session still pays for the whole history (at cached rates).
MCP tool definitions are deferred by default; still, disable unused servers and prefer CLI tools.
Hooks can preprocess output (e.g. grep a log) and skills can replace exploratory file reads; move specialised CLAUDE.md content to skills.
Delegate verbose operations to subagents; agent teams use roughly 7x the tokens of a standard session.

sources.title: Create custom subagents
sources.summary: Documents subagents as isolated context windows that return results to the main conversation.
keyPoints: Each subagent has its own context window, system prompt, tools and permissions.
Intended for side tasks that would flood the main conversation; returns only the summary.
Many subagents returning detailed results can consume significant main context.
The description field decides delegation.

sources.title: Hooks reference
sources.summary: Reference for hook events, inputs and how hook output reaches the model.
keyPoints: SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit plain-text stdout is added to Claude's context.
additionalContext, systemMessage and plain stdout are capped at 10,000 characters.
Over the cap, output is saved to a file and replaced by a path plus a preview of up to 2,000 characters.

sources.title: Explore the context window
sources.summary: Interactive walkthrough of what fills Claude Code's context at startup and during a session, and what survives compaction.
keyPoints: System prompt, CLAUDE.md, memory, skill listing and MCP tool names all load before the first prompt; MCP schemas stay deferred by default.
For PostToolUse hooks, plain stdout on exit 0 goes to the debug log, not the context; additionalContext does enter.
After compaction, root CLAUDE.md and memory are re-injected; path-scoped rules and hook-added context are summarised away; up to five recent files are re-read.
Subagent file reads never touch the parent's window; only the summary returns.

sources.title: How Claude Code uses prompt caching
sources.summary: Explains Claude Code's prefix-cache layout and which user actions invalidate it.
keyPoints: Every message re-sends the full context; the cache matches an exact prefix, so an early change recomputes everything after it.
Invalidators: model switch, effort change (most models), fast mode, MCP/plugin changes when tools load upfront, compaction, image eviction, upgrades.
Editing CLAUDE.md mid-session neither invalidates the cache nor applies until /clear, /compact or restart.
A subagent's first request does not read the parent's cache; a fork does.

sources.title: Extend Claude with skills
sources.summary: Reference for SKILL.md format, frontmatter, the skill listing budget and troubleshooting.
keyPoints: The description is what Claude uses to decide when to load a skill; if omitted, the first non-empty body line is used.
Combined description + when_to_use is truncated at 1,536 characters; the whole listing has a budget of ~1% of the window and drops descriptions of least-used skills on overflow.
Malformed frontmatter YAML: the skill loads with empty metadata, so /skill-name works but Claude cannot match on description.
Every listed skill adds to context on every turn whether or not it is used.

sources.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
sources.summary: MCP configuration in Claude Code, including tool search (deferred definitions) and output limits.
keyPoints: Tool search is the default: tool names are listed, full schemas load on demand.
Tool search is unavailable with a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, when disabled, or on some older models; then all definitions load upfront.
Warns when an MCP output exceeds 10,000 tokens; default maximum 25,000 tokens, with oversize results saved to a file.

sources.title: Manage sessions
sources.summary: How resume, continue, branch and transcripts work in Claude Code.
keyPoints: A resumed session restores full history including tool calls and results.
For large idle sessions (>100k tokens, ~1h), Claude Code offers resume-from-summary because the cache has expired and full history would be reprocessed.
Summaries cost less per request but whatever they omit leaves Claude's context.

sources.title: Tools reference
sources.summary: Per-tool behaviour of Claude Code's built-in tools, including built-in output caps.
keyPoints: A whole-file Read past the token limit returns a first page with a PARTIAL view notice and offset/limit guidance.
Glob results are capped at 100 files with a truncation flag; Grep supports head_limit.
Bash output is inline up to roughly 30,000 characters by default, then a file path plus preview.

sources.title: Prompt caching (Claude API)
sources.summary: API reference for prefix caching, its pricing and invalidation hierarchy.
keyPoints: Cache writes cost 1.25x base input (5-minute TTL) or 2x (1-hour); reads cost 0.1x (lower on some newer models).
Prefix order is tools, then system, then messages; changing tool definitions invalidates everything after.
Prompts below a model-specific minimum (512-4,096 tokens) cannot be cached.

sources.title: Context windows (Claude API)
sources.summary: Explains what counts toward the context window and why more context is not automatically better.
keyPoints: "more context isn't automatically better"; accuracy and recall degrade as tokens grow (context rot).
System prompt, all messages including tool results, and tool definitions all count toward the window.
Cached prefixes still occupy the window: caching changes price, not size.

sources.title: Context editing (Claude API)
sources.summary: API feature that clears old tool results (and optionally tool inputs) as a conversation grows.
keyPoints: Older tool results such as file contents or search results are no longer needed once processed.
Clearing replaces results with placeholders, oldest first; tool call inputs can be cleared too.
Clearing invalidates cached prefixes, so clear enough tokens at once to be worth it.

sources.title: Compaction overview (Claude API)
sources.summary: Server-side summarisation of older turns to keep long conversations inside the window.
keyPoints: Compaction keeps active context small because response quality degrades as a conversation grows.
Offers a custom summarisation prompt for when the default summary drops something a later turn needs.
Recent turns can be kept verbatim while older ones are summarised.

sources.title: Token counting (Claude API)
sources.summary: Free endpoint to count input tokens (system, tools, messages) before sending a request.
keyPoints: Counts are estimates and may differ slightly from billed input.
Claude Opus 4.7+ tokenizer yields roughly 30% more tokens for the same text than earlier models.
Recount per target model rather than reusing counts.

sources.title: Code execution with MCP: building more efficient agents
sources.authors: Adam Jones, Conor Kelly
sources.summary: Shows that loading many tool definitions and piping intermediate results through the model wastes context.
keyPoints: Tool definitions loaded upfront can mean hundreds of thousands of tokens before reading a request.
Intermediate results passing through the model repeatedly add large token costs.
Example workflow dropped from 150,000 to 2,000 tokens with code execution.

sources.title: Introducing advanced tool use on the Claude Developer Platform
sources.authors: Bin Wu et al.
sources.summary: Quantifies MCP tool-definition overhead and introduces the Tool Search Tool.
keyPoints: "58 tools consuming approximately 55K tokens before the conversation even starts".
Per server: GitHub ~26K tokens for 35 tools; Slack ~21K for 11 tools.
Deferring definitions via tool search cut token use ~85% and improved tool-selection accuracy in their evals.

sources.title: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills
sources.authors: Barry Zhang, Keith Lazuka, Mahesh Murag
sources.summary: Introduces Agent Skills and their progressive-disclosure loading model.
keyPoints: Only name and description are preloaded; they decide when a skill activates.
Full SKILL.md loads on relevance; bundled files load only as needed.

sources.title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
sources.authors: Justin Young
sources.summary: Describes progress files and git history so fresh context windows can pick up multi-session work.
keyPoints: "compaction isn't sufficient" on its own for multi-window builds.
A progress notes file plus git log lets a new session recover state quickly.

sources.title: Agent Skills specification
sources.summary: Open format spec for SKILL.md directories and frontmatter.
keyPoints: name (1-64 chars, lowercase/digits/hyphens, matches directory) and description (1-1024 chars, non-empty) are required.
Description should say what the skill does and when to use it, with task keywords.
Metadata ~100 tokens at startup; SKILL.md body recommended under 5,000 tokens / 500 lines.

sources.title: Custom instructions with AGENTS.md (Codex)
sources.summary: How Codex discovers and concatenates AGENTS.md files.
keyPoints: Global then project files are concatenated root-down; closer files appear later and take precedence.
project_doc_max_bytes defaults to 32 KiB; Codex stops adding files once the combined size hits it.
Empty files are skipped.

sources.title: Codex configuration reference
sources.summary: Reference for Codex config.toml keys, including context-related limits.
keyPoints: tool_output_token_limit budgets how much of each tool output is stored in history.
model_auto_compact_token_limit sets the compaction trigger.
MCP servers support enabled_tools / disabled_tools lists.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol in Codex
sources.summary: Configuring MCP servers in Codex, including per-server tool filtering and output budgets.
keyPoints: Per-server allowlist (enabled_tools) and denylist (disabled_tools).
Per-tool output token budget to limit how much context a response consumes.

sources.title: AGENTS.md
sources.summary: The open AGENTS.md format for giving coding agents project instructions.
keyPoints: A predictable place for build, test and style instructions for agents.
Nested files in monorepos; the closest file takes precedence.
Treat it as living documentation kept current with the project.

sources.title: Prompt caching (OpenAI API)
sources.summary: OpenAI's automatic exact-prefix prompt caching for prompts of 1,024+ tokens.
keyPoints: Requires an exact prefix match; put static instructions first and dynamic content last.
Cached reads are billed at a fraction of uncached input and reduce latency.

sources.title: Provide context with GEMINI.md files
sources.summary: How Gemini CLI loads hierarchical GEMINI.md context files.
keyPoints: Context files are concatenated and sent "to the model with every prompt".
Global, workspace and just-in-time files; /memory show displays the concatenation.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol specification: Tools (2025-06-18)
sources.summary: Defines how MCP servers list and describe tools to clients.
keyPoints: Each tool carries a name, description and JSON Schema inputSchema (optional outputSchema) returned by tools/list.
Servers can notify clients when the tool list changes (listChanged).

sources.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
sources.authors: Nelson F. Liu, Kevin Lin, John Hewitt, Ashwin Paranjape, Michele Bevilacqua, Fabio Petroni, Percy Liang
sources.summary: Shows long-context models use information at the start and end of the input far better than in the middle.
keyPoints: Accuracy is U-shaped over position of the relevant information.
Performance drops significantly when the needed fact sits in the middle of a long context.

sources.title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?
sources.authors: Cheng-Ping Hsieh, Simeng Sun, Samuel Kriman, Shantanu Acharya, Dima Rekesh, Fei Jia, Yang Zhang, Boris Ginsburg
sources.summary: Synthetic benchmark showing effective context is often much shorter than advertised.
keyPoints: Of models claiming 32K+ contexts, only about half held satisfactory performance at 32K.
Degradation grows with length and task complexity beyond simple needle retrieval.

sources.title: Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance
sources.authors: Kelly Hong, Anton Troynikov, Jeff Huber
sources.summary: Technical report on 18 LLMs showing reliability falls as input length grows, even on simple tasks.
keyPoints: Performance varies significantly with input length even on trivial tasks.
Even a single distractor lowers accuracy.
LongMemEval: focused ~300-token prompts beat full ~113k-token prompts by a wide margin.

sources.title: NoLiMa: Long-Context Evaluation Beyond Literal Matching
sources.authors: Ali Modarressi, Hanieh Deilamsalehy, Franck Dernoncourt, Trung Bui, Ryan A. Rossi, Seunghyun Yoon, Hinrich Schütze
sources.summary: Needle tests without lexical overlap reveal steep long-context degradation.
keyPoints: At 32K, 11 models fell below 50% of their short-context baseline.
GPT-4o dropped from 99.3% to 69.7%.

sources.title: Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance Despite Perfect Retrieval
sources.authors: Yufeng Du, Minyang Tian, Srikanth Ronanki, et al.
sources.summary: Shows sheer input length degrades reasoning even when the relevant evidence is perfectly retrieved.
keyPoints: Performance fell 13.9%-85% with longer inputs across five models on math, QA and coding.
Having the model recite the evidence first partially mitigates the drop.

sources.title: LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation
sources.authors: Philippe Laban, Hiroaki Hayashi, Yingbo Zhou, Jennifer Neville
sources.summary: Multi-turn, underspecified conversations cause large and unrecoverable quality drops.
keyPoints: Average 39% performance drop across six tasks versus single-turn.
Models commit to early assumptions and rarely recover from a wrong turn.

sources.title: On the Impact of AGENTS.md Files on the Efficiency of AI Coding Agents
sources.authors: Jai Lal Lulla, Seyedmoein Mohsenimofidi, Matthias Galster, Jie M. Zhang, Sebastian Baltes, Christoph Treude
sources.summary: Paired with/without AGENTS.md runs of Codex on 124 PRs from 10 repositories.
keyPoints: With AGENTS.md: median runtime -28.64%, output tokens -16.58%, completion comparable.
Limits: one agent (Codex), small PRs (<=100 LOC, <=5 files), light correctness checks, output tokens only.

sources.title: Evaluating AGENTS.md: Are Repository-Level Context Files Helpful for Coding Agents?
sources.authors: Thibaud Gloaguen, Niels Mündler, Mark Müller, Veselin Raychev, Martin Vechev
sources.summary: Across agents and models, context files did not generally raise success but raised inference cost.
keyPoints: Context files do "not generally improve task success rates" and raise inference cost by over 20%.
Agents follow context-file instructions well, so unnecessary requirements make tasks harder.
Repository overviews were ineffective; files help most for non-standard practices.

sources.title: What Keeps Agent Skills from Being Reusable? Evidence from 138K SKILL.md Files
sources.authors: Chi Zhang, Yimin Liu, Xinze Chen, Ping Ji
sources.summary: Large-scale audit of public SKILL.md files, dominated by routing-metadata defects.
keyPoints: 91.8% of skills have at least one defect; 67.0% have a routing (description) defect.
Missing trigger guidance (52.3%), overlong (14.3%) and non-functional (13.5%) descriptions are common.
In a BM25 routing test, clean-metadata skills hit@1 88.5% vs 82.6% for defective ones.

sources.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
sources.authors: John Yang, Carlos E. Jimenez, Alexander Wettig, Kilian Lieret, Shunyu Yao, Karthik Narasimhan, Ofir Press
sources.summary: Shows interface design (concise, bounded tool output) materially changes coding-agent success.
keyPoints: Search returns at most 50 results; beyond that the agent is told to refine the query.
File viewer of 100 lines beat full-file display (18.0% vs 12.7% resolved) and 30 lines (14.3%).
Observations older than the last five are collapsed to a single line.

sources.title: The Complexity Trap: Simple Observation Masking Is as Efficient as LLM Summarization for Agent Context Management
sources.authors: Tobias Lindenbauer, Igor Slinko, Ludwig Felder, Egor Bogomolov, Yaroslav Zharov
sources.summary: On SWE-bench Verified, masking old tool observations matches LLM summarisation at lower cost.
keyPoints: Observation masking roughly halves cost versus unmanaged context.
Solve rates equal or slightly better than LLM summarisation; a hybrid adds 7-11% efficiency.

sources.title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
sources.authors: Qizheng Zhang et al.
sources.summary: Identifies brevity bias and context collapse when contexts are repeatedly rewritten or summarised.
keyPoints: Brevity bias: concise summaries drop domain insights.
Context collapse: iterative rewriting erodes details over time.

sources.title: Don't Break the Cache: An Evaluation of Prompt Caching for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks
sources.authors: Elias Lumer, Faheem Nizar, Akshaya Jangiti, Kevin Frank, Anmol Gulati, Mandar Phadate, Vamse Kumar Subbiah
sources.summary: Measures prompt-caching savings for agents across OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.
keyPoints: Caching cut API cost 41-80% and time-to-first-token 13-31% over 500+ sessions.
Keeping dynamic content at the end and excluding dynamic tool results beats naive full-context caching.

sources.title: Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus
sources.authors: Yichao 'Peak' Ji
sources.summary: Production lessons on cache-friendly, append-only agent context.
keyPoints: "KV-cache hit rate is the single most important metric" for production agents.
Keep prefixes stable (no timestamps), append-only, and mask tools instead of removing them.
Compress restorably (keep the URL/path, drop the content); keep failed actions visible.

sources.title: Don't Build Multi-Agents
sources.authors: Walden Yan
sources.summary: Argues context splitting across agents causes conflicting implicit decisions.
keyPoints: Share context and full agent traces, not just individual messages.
Actions carry implicit decisions; parallel agents without shared context make conflicting ones.
Suggests a dedicated model to compress history into key details and decisions.

sources.title: Context Engineering for Agents
sources.authors: LangChain team
sources.summary: Groups context techniques into write, select, compress and isolate.
keyPoints: Tool feedback accumulates across turns and can exceed or degrade the window.
Isolation (sub-agents) and compression are complementary levers.

sources.title: How Long Contexts Fail
sources.authors: Drew Breunig
sources.summary: Names four long-context failure modes with cited examples.
keyPoints: Poisoning, distraction, confusion (superfluous tools/content) and clash (conflicting content).
Cites a Gemini agent past ~100k tokens repeating past actions instead of planning.
Cites evidence that adding tools degrades function-calling accuracy.

sources.title: Context engineering
sources.authors: Simon Willison
sources.summary: Records the adoption of 'context engineering', quoting Tobi Lutke and Andrej Karpathy.
keyPoints: Karpathy: the job is filling the window with just the right information.
Links Karpathy's original post (x.com/karpathy/status/1937902205765607626), not fetched directly.

sources.title: dotagents-standard: an agent skill for the .agents layout
sources.authors: Jeff Mixon
sources.summary: Describes a slim AGENTS.md router plus a .agents/ directory loaded by progressive disclosure.
keyPoints: Keep the root instruction file a router; pull rules, context, specs on demand.
Separates standing rules from evolving memory and task specs.
Instruction files grow until nobody, human or model, reads them end to end.

sources.title: Edit formats
sources.summary: Compares whole-file and diff edit formats for LLM code edits.
keyPoints: Whole-file edits are "slow and costly" because the model returns the entire file.
Diff formats return only changed parts.

B-01.note: Vendors cap and paginate tool output because large results consume context, and position effects are documented; the 'tenth of the window' threshold is our opinion.
caveats: Claude Code already bounds single results (MCP 25k tokens, Bash ~30k chars inline, Read partial view), persisting overflow to a file, so an unbounded single result is rarer than the rationale implies.
'Until compaction' is not always true: API context editing and Claude Code tool-result clearing can remove old results earlier.
Lost in the Middle shows a U-shaped curve; content after the instructions does not strictly 'push' them out, it moves them away from the recency end.

B-02.note: Claude Code docs say to encode repeated corrections in CLAUDE.md and to preprocess output with hooks; calling repetition a 'habit signal' is our interpretation.
caveats: CLAUDE.md is advisory; a hook or tool-level limit is deterministic (cc-best-practices), so 'fix it in instructions once' may not hold.

B-03.note: SWE-agent shows windowed views beat full-file display and vendors recommend range reads; the claim that generated files are 'the most common cause' of window jumps is unsourced opinion.
caveats: Claude Code's Read already returns a partial first page for files over its token limit, so the worst case is bounded per call.

B-04.note: Every tool result counts toward the window and redundant results are the first thing vendors clear; the specific rule is our inference.
caveats: Re-running a call after the file or state changed is legitimate: Claude Code appends a file-changed reminder and expects a re-read when needed.

B-05.note: Anthropic states subagents should return condensed summaries (often 1,000-2,000 tokens) and that detailed returns consume main context; our exact size threshold is opinion.
caveats: Cognition argues over-compressed handoffs lose implicit decisions; too-thin handoffs have a quality cost, so passing file references (multi-agent post) may beat plain shortening.

B-06.note: Docs confirm a subagent starts with its own context (no parent cache, no parent memory), so it must re-acquire what it needs; labelling those reads as waste is our inference.
caveats: The child genuinely lacks the parent's content; 'without adding information' holds only for the combined system. Cognition's advice is to share context, not forbid the read.
Claude Code forks inherit the parent context and cache, which is the documented alternative.

B-07.note: Anthropic and ACE document information loss from summarisation and repeated rewriting; 'theory' proving no lossless summary is not sourced, and the frequency threshold is opinion.
caveats: Vendors present compaction as the primary strategy for long contexts because quality degrades as context grows; compaction is also a remedy.
Lindenbauer et al. find summarisation does not lower solve rates versus masking, so loss does not always hurt outcomes.

B-08.note: Degradation with input length before the hard limit is well supported; 'the last 20% of the window' is our opinion.
caveats: Research measures degradation by absolute length (e.g. 32K, 113K), not by fraction of the window; on a 1M window 80% full is 800K tokens, far beyond most tested ranges.

B-09.note: Pricing (writes 1.25-2x, reads 0.1x) and prefix-invalidation behaviour are documented; the churn threshold is opinion.
caveats: Some misses are expected rather than upstream bugs: compaction, idle past TTL, model/effort switches; Claude Code counts compaction rebuilds separately from misses.

B-10.note: Docs show substantial startup load and advise trimming it; 'a quarter of the window' is our threshold.
caveats: The stable system prefix is usually cached at ~0.1x, so its cost impact is smaller than its share of the window.
Claude Code defers MCP schemas by default, removing the largest historical contributor.

B-11.note: Claude Code docs state a one-line question in a long session still draws usage for the whole conversation; what counts as 'tiny' is our opinion.
caveats: With a warm cache the resent history bills at the cached rate, so the monetary impact is roughly an order of magnitude below raw token counts.

B-12.note: Old tool outputs are documented as the safest content to clear or mask, with cost halved and no solve-rate loss in one study; the dominance ratio is opinion.
caveats: Clearing tool results invalidates the prompt cache, so clear in batches.
Manus recommends keeping failed actions and errors visible; not all results are equally compressible.

B-13.note: Vendor docs recommend /clear and fresh sessions with notes, and multi-turn research shows unrecoverable drift; the length threshold is opinion.
caveats: Claude Code best practices say it is sometimes right to let context accumulate when deep in one problem; 'cheaper and more accurate' is not universal.

B-14.note: SWE-agent caps search at 50 results and asks for a narrower query; Claude Code caps Glob at 100 files; the flood threshold is opinion.
caveats: SWE-agent's 'iterative search' (one hit at a time) performed worse than no search, so over-restricting results also hurts.

B-15.note: Anthropic reports agents duplicate work without detailed task descriptions and multi-agent runs use ~15x chat tokens; the detection heuristic is ours.

B-16.note: Docs confirm hook output, mid-conversation system reminders and resumed history enter the request; whether they are visible in the log is our observation about transcript formats.
caveats: Resumed history is in the transcript; the cost is real but 'not visible' applies only to injections the log format omits.

B-17.note: Tool call inputs remain in history (the API offers to clear them) and whole-file rewrites are known to be costly; the dominance threshold is opinion.
caveats: Aider's point is output cost and latency, not input persistence; the persistence claim rests on how message history works.

H-01.note: Docs say to write recurring corrections into CLAUDE.md and to bound or preprocess output; 'one line prevents it every time' is our claim.
caveats: CLAUDE.md is advisory with no compliance guarantee (cc-memory); a hook or tool limit is the deterministic fix.

H-02.note: Vendor docs suggest skills or notes instead of exploratory reads, and SWE-agent favours windowed views; the cross-session rule is ours.
caveats: Claude Code best practices advise against file-by-file descriptions in CLAUDE.md; name a range or a 'do not read', not a summary of code.

H-03.note: Subagent behaviour comes from its definition's system prompt, and Anthropic says delegations need an explicit output format; putting the fix in the definition is our inference.

H-04.note: No source discusses compaction frequency trends; the docs only explain what fills the window and triggers compaction.

H-05.note: Instruction files load on every session and sit in the cached project-context layer; flagging edits that move the base is our design.
caveats: A chars-per-token estimate is model-dependent: Anthropic says newer tokenizers produce ~30% more tokens for the same text, so the local estimate can drift.

H-06.note: Claude Code docs say to disable unused servers; per-server schema costs are documented by Anthropic.
caveats: In Claude Code, MCP schemas are deferred by default: only tool names and server instructions go on every request. 'Pays its schema cost on every request' holds only when tool search is off or unavailable (custom base URL, some older models).

H-07.note: Docs support memory, notes and skills that replace repeated exploration; replacing a specific file read is our inference.
caveats: Gloaguen et al. found repository overviews in context files ineffective, and Claude Code auto memory deliberately skips facts derivable from code; summarising code into instructions can go stale and add cost.
Re-reading guarantees freshness when the file changes between sessions.

S-01.note: Vendors say instruction files load every session and long files reduce adherence (Claude Code: target <200 lines; Codex: 32 KiB cap); our token threshold is opinion.
caveats: Claude Code delivers CLAUDE.md as a user message after the system prompt, not in it.
It sits in a cached prefix, so the per-turn price is ~0.1x after the first request; the attention cost remains.

S-02.note: Claude Code docs say contradictory rules may be resolved arbitrarily and warn that duplicate AGENTS.md loading adds a second copy.

S-03.note: The description is the documented routing key, required by the spec, and routing-metadata defects measurably reduce retrieval.
caveats: Claude Code falls back to the first non-empty body line when description is missing, so 'never loads' is overstated for Claude Code.
The defect study's retrieval test used BM25, not a live agent, and the gap was modest (88.5% vs 82.6% hit@1).

S-04.note: Claude Code loads skills with malformed YAML without metadata so auto-matching fails; the spec sets name/description constraints.
caveats: Truncation comes from the 1,536-char listing cap and listing budget, not from malformed metadata; the skill remains invokable by /name, so it is not invisible.

S-05.note: Claude Code's prompt audit explicitly flags references to missing files and agents follow instructions closely; 'one failed call per session' is our estimate.

S-06.note: Path-scoped rules load only when matching files are read; skills and routers give on-demand loading.
caveats: Path-scoped rules are summarised away at compaction until a matching file is read again; rules that must persist belong unscoped.

S-07.note: Docs advise removing outdated instructions and keeping files current; Gloaguen shows agents follow instructions, so stale ones steer behaviour; how staleness is detected is our heuristic.

S-08.note: Anthropic reports single MCP servers costing ~21-26K tokens, which can exceed a typical CLAUDE.md.
caveats: In Claude Code, tool definitions are deferred by default via tool search, so 'every tool schema is prompt text on every request' is false unless tool search is disabled or unavailable; it remains true for clients that load schemas upfront.

S-09.note: Claude Code docs explicitly recommend disabling servers you are not using.
caveats: With deferred tools the residual cost is tool names and server instructions, much smaller than full schemas.

S-10.note: Vendor posts support persistent notes to avoid re-discovery; that absence of memory causes repeated tool calls is our inference.
caveats: Claude Code auto memory is on by default and writes itself; an empty memory directory may just mean nothing was worth saving.

S-11.note: SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit stdout and additionalContext enter context; size threshold is opinion.
caveats: Overstated as written: plain stdout of PostToolUse hooks on exit 0 goes to the debug log, not context, and injected hook text is capped at 10,000 chars with the rest moved to a file.

S-12.note: One study (Codex, 124 small PRs) found AGENTS.md lowered runtime and output tokens; another broader study disagrees.
caveats: Gloaguen et al. found context files do not generally improve success and raise inference cost >20% across agents and models; 'evidence shows' should become 'evidence is mixed'.
